## Goal

Pin the off-peak-windowed, all-opencode low-priority fallback behaviour with tests **before** the config change (test-first).

## Scope

Tests only; no production behaviour change in this item.

## Work

1. **Window gating:** an `available_times`-carrying entry is skipped outside its UTC window (`_is_within_allowed_window` → `Skipping provider=...: outside its available_times window (UTC)`) and selected inside it.
2. **Chain order:** `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code resolves to `local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`. (Red until the config item lands — intended TDD state; document the convention if the repo requires green main.)
3. **Per-key 429 failover (the key behaviour):** a 429 from `opencode-go-3` must NOT exclude `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` from the same request — rate-limit quarantine is keyed on `_usage_limit_account_key` (`api_key_env@endpoint`), so sibling accounts are independent (LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
4. **Same-domain 5xx caveat:** a 5xx from `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude its same-gateway siblings as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) — assert the honest behaviour so nobody assumes 3× outage resilience.
5. **No paid-tier leak:** `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in any `low` chain.
6. **Medium/high unaffected:** those chains are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests cover in-window selection, out-of-window skip-and-fall-through, and behaviour-neutrality when the free tier still has budget.
2. A test asserts the exact 5-entry low chain order for plan, author and code.
3. A test asserts 429-per-account failover lets sibling opencode keys be tried in the same request.
4. A test asserts 5xx does NOT give sibling failover (same failure domain).
5. A test asserts `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` absent from `low` chains and `medium`/`high` chains unchanged.
6. Reuses existing proxy test conventions (monkeypatched clock for `available_times`, existing timing-gate fixtures) rather than inventing new harness code.
7. full suite green via `/skill:test`, except the documented intentional red chain-order assertion pending the config item.
data.title: Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating

data.description:
# Tests: reset-aware account quarantine (test-first, red)

## Goal

As a proxy operator, I want failing tests that pin down the reset-aware,
account-scoped 429 quarantine, so the implementation in the sibling item is
driven by executable expectations rather than prose.

## Parent context

Parent LP-0MVDNP36J006430L ("Respect MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* reset headers on
quota 429s") owns the **account-scoped application** of the reset-derived
cooldown. The generic header-parsing engine already landed in
LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (completed, commit `1245f383`): `_parse_ratelimit_duration`,
`_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `_ratelimit_over_limit`,
`_get_respect_ratelimit_headers`, and the provider-entry cooldown applied in
`_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`. LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (completed) supplied
account-key eligibility: `_is_account_rate_limit_error`,
`_usage_limit_account_key`, and per-request `attempted_domains` poisoning.

**Gap this phase pins down:** a quota 429 carrying a reset header currently
sets only the provider-ENTRY cooldown (`mark_provider_unavailable(name, …)`,
2 s margin, 60 s cap) and never records an account-scoped quarantine in
`_usage_reset_at`. So the reset duration is not persisted, not reflected in
`_compute_retry_after()`, and does not cover a differently-named entry
sharing the same `api_key_env` account.

## Scope

Tests only — no production code changes in this item. New tests must be
**red** (failing) against current `dev` and the red output must be recorded
in a comment before moving on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A test writes a quota 429 body (`type: rate_limit_error`,
      `code: rate_limit_exceeded`) plus `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 32s`
      (and `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes`) from a `munitoai-free`-style entry
      with `respect_ratelimit_headers: true`, and asserts the failing
      ACCOUNT key is quarantined in `_usage_reset_at` with
      `_usage_reset_remaining(account) > 0` and an expiry of roughly
      `now + 32 + 120` seconds (parsed reset + the existing
      `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` 2-minute margin).
- [ ] AC2 — A test asserts the quarantine is scoped to the failing
      `api_key_env` account key ONLY: the paid sibling
      (`MUNITOAI_API_KEY`-style account) has no `_usage_reset_at` entry, no
      provider cooldown, and `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions` still
      returns it after the 429 (sibling preservation,
      LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
- [ ] AC3 — A test asserts a quota 429 carrying a reset header advances the
      chain to the next provider within the same request, and that a quota
      429 exhausting the whole chain still produces the chain-hold
      exhaustion response with a `retry_after` derived from the account
      quarantine (i.e. `_compute_retry_after()` sees `_usage_reset_at`).
- [ ] AC4 — A test asserts unchanged behaviour when no reset signal is
      present: a quota 429 with no `x-ratelimit-*` headers applies the
      existing short provider cooldown, creates NO `_usage_reset_at` entry,
      and poisons only the per-request account key (not the failure domain).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression tests confirm the `FreeUsageLimitError` (3 h
      cooldown) and `GoUsageLimitError` (account quarantine) paths are
      unchanged by the new code path.
- [ ] AC6 — A test asserts the feature-flag gate: with
      `respect_ratelimit_headers` false on the entry (and not enabled
      globally) the reset headers are ignored and no account quarantine is
      created.
- [ ] AC7 — Both fallback loops are covered:
      `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`
      each have at least one reset-aware quarantine assertion, so a fix
      applied to only one loop fails the suite.
- [ ] AC8 — The red test run is recorded in a comment on this work item
      (command + failing test names) before the implementation item starts.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` with the focused
  quarantine/`Retry-After`/flag-gate cases (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7).
- Reuse the existing fixtures and 429 builders in
  `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` (`munitoai_free_paid_chain`,
  `_rate_limit_exceeded_429`) — extend that file for the sibling-eligibility
  case (AC2) rather than duplicating fixtures.
- Use the existing autouse reset fixtures (module-level `_usage_reset_at` /
  `_provider_unavailable_until` clearing) so tests stay order-independent.

## Constraints

- Do NOT re-implement header parsing — call the existing helpers.
- Do NOT weaken or delete the existing account-key poisoning assertions
  (notably `test_account_429_poisons_account_key_not_failure_domain`, whose
  `free_account not in provider._usage_reset_at` assertion must stay valid
  for a reset-header-less 429).
- Tests must not require network access or a live proxy.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` — new focused test module
  for the reset-aware account quarantine.
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — sibling-eligibility and
  per-request exclusion assertions.
- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_headers_cooldown.py` — existing header-parsing
  and provider-cooldown tests that must keep passing.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference for the helpers under test.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first). Blocks the implementation item.

## Deliverables

- New/extended tests, red against current `dev`.
- Red-run evidence recorded as a work-item comment.
data.title: Tests: reset-aware account quarantine (test-first)
